A systemd scope seems like overkill to me.

fields.summary: On 2026-11-17 the owner asked that the daemon run any workflow, built-in or bring-your-own, from start to finish with intervention the exception, so the orchestrator session beside it becomes unnecessary. The orchestrator's brief listed what it does by hand today: machine rules sent to conductors, a stall watch, tmp sweeps, setting maxRuns by hand, retrying failed runs, and handing notes to planners. The planner asked four questions, and the owner answered through the orchestrator's chat. (1) Host limits: no systemd scopes or cgroups, which are Linux-only, and no daemon test-slot count. Instead the daemon's load, memory and disk holds also gate every child session spawn and add a free-tmp hold, and the stall watchdog treats a runaway session (its process tree's process count or memory past a host threshold, read portably) like a stall. The /tmp projection leak (01M7M3JZFW) and the 2.2 GB RSS of ship open-pr stay bug fixes. (2) Failed runs restart at the step the workflow names (default: the failed step; a plan refused by review-check restarts at plan), with the failure's output and findings in the next attempt's brief, one retry by default, then the inbox. (3) rhiza.daemon.maxRuns=auto starts another run only while the pre-start checks have room; a number still pins it. (4) The push wake-up draft 01M7M2FB5B serves this milestone; the check-in alarms of 01M7M2FE1S fold into the daemon's stall detection, and that draft is withdrawn. The planner ruled on what was left unasked: the order against the web split, the done measure, and planning each change set's leaves in its own plan run.
fields.title: Milestone 40 interview: the daemon runs any workflow, with the owner
